WHEREAS, the Town Council of the Town of Clermont, Georgia is authorized by Art. IX, § Il, J Il of the Constitution of the State of Georgia of 1983, and the Town Charter to regulate noise; and

WHEREAS, the Town Council finds that it is in the best interests of the health, safety, and welfare of the Town citizens to regulate noise; and

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Town Council of Clermont, Georgia, and it is hereby ordained by the above authority, as follows:
11: This ordinance shall be titled the "Town of Clermont Noise Ordinance"
13:
- (a) Purpose and intent. This ordinance is enacted to protect, preserve and promote the health, safety and welfare of the citizens of the Town of Clermont, Georgia, through the control of noise, a recognized form of environmental pollution. It is the intent of this

ordinance to establish objective standards that will reduce excessive community noises, which are harmful and otherwise detrimental to individuals and to the community in the enjoyment of life and property and in the conduct of business. It is not the intent of this ordinance to regulate noise based upon its source, but based upon objective volume limitations at objective distances from the source, which for purposes of this ordinance intentionally vary based upon the time of day and reasonable expectations of persons occupying the area during the relevant time period. It is not the intent of this ordinance to regulate speech, under either the Federal or Georgia Constitutions. This ordinance has been narrowly tailored as a content-neutral time, place, and manner regulation to serve a significant governmental interest while leaving open ample opportunity for communication.

- (b) Definition of "noise". For purposes of this ordinance, "noise" means a sound or sounds of any kind, that is repetitive or continuous, and of sufficient duration, that a person of reasonable auditory sensitivity would consider loud, unpleasant, unexpected, or undesirable.

- (c) Sound measurement standards. For the purposes of this ordinance, "plainly audible" shall mean any sound emanating from a specific sound-producing source which can be heard from the distances set forth below, using the following sound measurement standards: Measurement shall be by the auditory senses of a person standing at a distance no less than the required minimum distance from the source of the sound. Inasmuch as the limitation on noise is neutral as to the content of the message, if any, generated or conveyed by its source, words and phrases need not be discernable. For music and other noise, bass reverberations are included.
14:
11:00 P.M. SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY AND 7:00 A.M. THROUGH 12:00 MIDNIGHT ON FRIDAY AND SATURDAY.

- (a) Except when noise emanates from a source exempted by this ordinance, it is a violation of this ordinance for any person or persons to sing, yell, shout, hoot, whistle, or play a musical instrument, on the public streets or sidewalks or on private property so as to create, or cause to be created, any noises or sounds which are plainly audible at a distance of 300 feet or more from the building, structure, or vehicle from which the sound is emanating, or when generated outdoors on real property, 300 feet beyond the boundary or property limits on which the person is located, between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 11:00 p.m. Sunday through Thursday and between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 12:00 midnight on Friday and Saturday.

- (b) Except when noise emanates from a source exempted by this ordinance, it is a violation of this ordinance for any person or persons to play, use, or operate any machine, appliance, tool, or device for the producing, reproducing, or amplifying of sound and/or noise at such a volume and in such a manner so as to create, or cause to be created, any noise or sounds which are plainly audible at a distance of 300 feet or more from the building, structure, or vehicle from which the sound is emanating, or when generated outdoors on real property, 300 feet beyond the property limits on which it is located, between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 11:00 p.m. Sunday through Thursday and between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 12:00 midnight on Friday and Saturday.
15:
MIDNIGHT ON SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY AND 12:00 MIDNIGHT THROUGH 7:00 A.M. DAILY.

- (a) Except when noise emanates from a source exempted by this ordinance, it is a violation of this ordinance for any person or persons to sing, yell, shout, hoot, whistle, or play

a musical instrument, on the public streets or sidewalks or on private property so as to create, or cause to be created, any noises or sounds which are plainly audible at a distance of 100 feet or more from the building, structure, or vehicle from which the sound is emanating, or when generated outdoors on real property, 100 feet beyond the boundary or property limits on which the person is located, between the hours of 11:00 p.m. to 12:00 midnight Sunday through Thursday and between the hours of 12:00 midnight to 7:00 a.m. daily.

- (b) Except when noise emanates from a source exempted by this ordinance, it is a violation of this ordinance for any person or persons to play, use, or operate any machine, appliance, tool, or device for the producing, reproducing, or amplifying of sound and/or noise at such a volume and in such a manner so as to create, or cause to be created, any noise or sounds which are plainly audible at a distance of 100 feet or more from the building, structure, or vehicle from which the sound is emanating, or when generated outdoors on real property, 100 feet beyond the property limits on which it is located, between the hours of 11:00 p.m. to 12:00 midnight Sunday through Thursday and between the hours of 12:00 midnight to 7:00 a.m. daily.

- (c) Except for persons operating within properly licensed or permitted nonresidential enterprises that have an adjoining property line or boundary with a residential dwelling unit, during the days and hours set forth in this section, it is a violation of this ordinance for any person to make, cause, or continue to make any noise in such a manner as to be plainly audible to any other person a distance of five feet beyond the adjoining wall or boundary of any apartment, condominium, townhouse, duplex, or other such residential dwelling units with adjoining points of contact. For the purposes of this section, "wall or boundary" shall mean an imaginary line drawn through the points of contact of (1) adjoining

apartments, condominiums, townhouses, duplexes or other such residential dwelling units with adjoining points owned, rented, or leased by different persons; or (2) adjoining common areas or adjoining exterior walls. Said property line or boundary includes all points of a plane formed by projecting the property line or boundary including the ceiling, the floor, and the walls.

Registration is required of all outdoor entertainment events that have live or recorded musical entertainment and/or that use electronic amplification. Registration of the event must be at least 72 hours prior to the event, and must be by the person or persons responsible for the event. Registration is to be with the Town of Clermont through the Town Clerk, Monday through Friday, from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., on an application specified by the Town and shall include the name, address, telephone number or other contact information for the person or organization sponsoring the event, the location, the date and time of the event, and security provisions. No fee shall be charged for registration and the Town may make provision for registration by telephone or online through the Town's website. Unless expressly approved by the Town Mayor, registration shall not be accepted for events that include the hours between 11:00 p.m. and 12:00 midnight Sunday through Thursday, and between 12:00 midnight and 7:00 a.m. daily. Failure to register an event may result in a fine, forfeiture of the right of future registrations, or both. Registration does not exempt the person or persons registering the event

from ensuring that the event complies with the requirements of this ordinance. Failure to register shall be a violation of this ordinance.
19: Any person violating the provisions of this ordinance shall be cited to appear before the municipal court, and upon conviction punished subject to the maximum penalties allowed by the Town Charter and as assessed by a court of competent jurisdiction provided, however, a violation of Section 6 for failure to register an outdoor entertainment event shall be punished only by a fine not to exceed $100.00.
20: This ordinance shall become effective upon passage.
21: All ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict herewith are hereby repealed to the extent of the conflict. Accrued fees imposed by prior ordinances in effect prior to the effective date of this ordinance shall continue to be owed to the Town of Clermont and shall not be affected by this ordinance.
22:
If any portion of this ordinance shall be invalid or unconstitutional, such invalidity or unconstitutionality shall not affect or impair the remaining portions unless it clearly appears that other parts are wholly and necessarily dependent upon the part held to be invalid or unconstitutional.
